basics.summary: I am currently an Analyst Developer at Smals seconded the the Belgian National Employment Office (NEO). I completed a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Sciences in 2020. work.name: Avanade
work.summary:
Avanade is the leading provider of innovative digital and cloud services, business solutions and design-led experiences delivered through the power of people and the Microsoft ecosystem. Majority owned by Accenture, Avanade was founded in 2000 by Accenture LLP and Microsoft Corporation.

The goal of the internship was to design, develop, and deploy Azure DevOps web extensions. They were intended to help a scrum software development team by improving the communication between its members. It did so by allowing developers to register their mood daily (in a Niko-Niko calendar fashion). The collected data was then compiled into reports. The resulting data visualization was then presented to the scrum master for her/him to take action upon a negative general mood.

The extensions frontend have been developed using React and TypeScript. A RESTful API was hosted using Microsoft Azure. The web application used different services: Azure Functions (C# and .NET), Azure Storage (Table), and Azure Key Vault. The project was developed using the Scrum framework on the Azure DevOps platform
highlights: Designed the Avanade's Mood Measuring Initiative (A.M.M.I.) project
Developed the solution using .NET, C#, Microsoft Azure, React and TypeScript
Managed the project development using the Scrum framework and Azure DevOps
Support the Belgian Employment Office mainframe migration to the cloud
Maintain and debug C++ shared libraries
Develop web applications using Angular and Spring Boot

projects.name: Awesome PS
projects.description: This is a simplistic implementation of the PS Linux command using the C programming language and the API provided by the proc virtual file system. The virtual file system was used to find information about the processes currently running on a system.

projects.name: Blokus
projects.description: I developed this game during the second year (december 2018) of my Bachelor's degree in computer sciences. This was an assignment for a course about the fundamentals of Software Development using Java. The course followed a first theoretical course about the Java programming language. During this unit, we have learned: object oriented programming fundamentals, lambdas, generics, and graphical user interface development using JavaFX.

projects.name: Journal de bord
projects.description: In the process of getting ready for the B driver's license, it is possible to obtain a temporary license. The keeper must keep a logbook (Journal de bord) that tracks his or her route, traffic conditions and possible encountered difficulties. Today, the logbook has to be kept by printing and completing documents manually. The documents are provided on the site of mobilite-mobiliteit.brussels. There are two of them: an overview of the rides and the details of a rides.  I was asked to hold a logbook myself. I can assure you that this is very demanding and takes a lot of time. This is why I find it useful to develop a mobile solution that automates (as far as possible) the the logbook.
